children.text: Isolated GGT: GGT above the lab's range for age; ALT and bilirubin normal. ALP may be raised too.
Use the lab's range for age: GGT is high in young infants and lowest at 1–6 years — below adult values.

children.cond: Fever with jaundice or right upper quadrant pain

pill.text: Emergency department now: blood cultures, ultrasound — cholangitis or a stone

children.cond: Direct bilirubin raised, jaundice, pale stools or itch
Vomiting blood, black stools or active bleeding
Large spleen or low platelets, no bleeding

pill.text: Hepatology within days: possible portal hypertension or advanced liver disease

children.cond: Carbamazepine, phenytoin or phenobarbital, child well
children.subtext: Likely enzyme induction — no workup (expert opinion). Recheck with routine drug monitoring; investigate if GGT keeps rising, or ALT or bilirubin rise

children.cond: Fever, rash or lymph nodes in the first months of a new drug

pill.text: Same day: think DRESS or drug-induced liver injury — CBC with eosinophils, ALT, INR
Not an inducer: ALT, INR and ammonia this week
Emergency department now: ammonia, ALT, INR, glucose

children.cond: Valproate with vomiting or lethargy; or under 2 years; or mitochondrial disease

pill.text: Same day: ALT, INR, ammonia (valproate boxed warning)

children.cond: Obese teen, suspected MASLD, GGT ≥ 60 U/L

pill.text: Full tier 1 now and pediatric hepatology — not MASLD until proven (ESPGHAN 2026)

children.cond: None, or obese with normal ALT

children.text: Repeat once with ALT, AST, ALP, bilirubin and platelets — within 3 months (expert opinion).
Still raised: abdominal ultrasound with Doppler; ANA, SMA, anti-LKM1, IgG; fecal calprotectin.
Examine for Alagille features: heart murmur, typical face, butterfly vertebrae, posterior embryotoxon. Sweat test if cystic fibrosis is possible.

children.cond: Abdominal pain with dilated ducts or stones
Dilated ducts or cyst, no pain

pill.text: Hepatology or surgery referral within days
Hepatology within 1–2 weeks: autoimmune hepatitis or autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis (expert opinion)
Pediatric GI: IBD workup; hepatology for MRCP
Hepatology referral: MRCP. Biopsy only if persistent > 6 months with a normal MRCP — hepatologist decision

children.text: Check GGT every 3–6 months in every child with IBD — PSC is often silent.

pill.text: Investigate promptly: MRCP and hepatology referral
Cause workup: drugs, viral serology, ANA, SMA, anti-LKM1, IgG. MRCP not routine; recheck GGT every 3–6 months

children.text: In the study behind the 2 × ULN cut-off, ULN was 50 U/L (2 × ULN = 100 U/L).
